Status.note: The Maryland Public Service Commission order of December 30, 2025 approved Constellation's Project 2, a 564 MW gas plant, for the expedited permit route. A June 29, 2026 letter order says Constellation has not yet applied for the permit and must apply by July 1, 2027. Nothing says construction has started. So the project is announced.

Capacity (MW).note: The Commission order of December 30, 2025 describes Project 2 as a 564 MW natural gas generation plant. The figure is a maximum output, not a stated nameplate rating.

Fuel.note: The order describes Project 2 as a natural gas plant. Its turbines can run on a hydrogen blend, but only natural gas is planned.

Turbine/Engine Technology.note: The order says Project 2 would be built with combustion gas turbines that Constellation already owns and would move to the new site, and that the turbines are air cooled. No steam turbine is mentioned.

Start year.note: The order notes that Constellation gave confidential timelines for a commercial operation date of June 1, 2029 for both gas projects. A Maryland Matters article from November 2025 reports the same target. This is a planned date, not an actual start.

Latest Activity.value: Approved for expedited permitting by the Maryland Public Service Commission in December 2025; permit application due by July 1, 2027
Latest Activity.note: The Commission letter order of June 29, 2026 directs Constellation to file its permit application for Projects 1 and 2 no later than July 1, 2027. The company expects to file by the end of June 2027 if gas supply conditions are met.

Status Detail.value: Approved for the state's expedited permit process; permit application not yet filed; target commercial operation June 2029
Status Detail.note: The June 29, 2026 Commission letter order says the permit application is still to come. The December 2025 order sets June 1, 2029 as the target operation date. The company also needs a gas pipeline extension that it priced at about 800 million dollars.

units.notes: Everything comes from the Maryland Public Service Commission orders on the Next Generation Energy Act. The orders give no turbine make, model or count, and no coordinates were reported. The turbines are already owned by Constellation and would be moved from other Constellation property. Project 2 is the 564 MW option.

Owner(s).note: The Commission order names Constellation Energy Generation, LLC as the applicant and says Constellation owns both the turbines and the site. No co-owners are mentioned.

Operator(s).note: The order names Constellation as the applicant. It does not name a separate operator, so this is implied.

qa.recommendation: Confirm that this record is Constellation Project 2, the 564 MW option, and that the two projects are meant to be separate records.
qa.note: The order calls the 150 MW plant Project 1 and the 564 MW plant Project 2. They are two alternative proposals for the same area near the Perryman Generating Station in Harford County. News reports say Constellation offered them as a menu of options, so only one may be built. Because the order redacts site details, the exact location is unknown.

qa.recommendation: Consider whether the start year of 2029 should be entered while the project is only announced.
qa.note: The 2029 date is the company's target operation date. The permit application had not been filed as of June 2026 and the gas supply is not settled.
